summary: Yoshifumi Honjo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Kyoto University. His career includes posts at Kyoto University, Bukkyo University, Kobe Women's University (2000–2004), and Otani University (attested 2010).

Yoshifumi Mizuno is an Indologist and linguist who studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies and the University of Tokyo. He served as an assistant at the University of Tokyo (1986–1992) and Associate Professor at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (2000–2024).

Yoshihide Yoshizu (1943–2014) was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar. He studied at Komazawa University under Shoson Miyamoto and Shigeo Kamata, later serving as Lecturer from 1971 and Professor from 2001 at Komazawa University.

Yoshihiko Amino (1929–2004) was a historian and Japanologist who studied at the University of Tokyo (circa 1947–1950). He held academic posts at Nagoya University (circa 1967–1980) and Kanagawa University (circa 1980–1998).

Yoshihiko Nasu is a scholar of Buddhist studies. His career includes positions as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 2007) and leadership roles at Kongojushinkai and Kongozyu (attested 2017).

Yoshihiko Sakurai is a Buddhist studies scholar who pursued doctoral studies at Ryukoku University (attested 2001). He has served as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 2003) and researcher at Jodo Shinshu Hongwanji-ha Kyogaku Dendo Kenkyu Center.
Yoshihiro Hayashi is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. In 2009, he was attested as a Professor at Ritsumeikan University and as a part-time Lecturer at Shitennoji University.
Yoshihiro Matsunami is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held a professorship at Taisho University (attested 1991–1999) and served as the university's president in 2001.

Yoshihito Muroji is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen, David Seyfort Ruegg, and Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan. He served at Koyasan University and Shiga University of Medical Science.
Yoshiki Motoaki is a scholar in the field of Buddhist studies. His career includes appointments with Otani University (attested 2013) and the Otani Academic Society (attested 2026).

Yoshimi Nozawa is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. As of 2026, he is attested as a part-time lecturer at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Yoshinobu Kimoto is a historian and Japanologist who studied at Komazawa, Meiji, and Tezukayama universities. He held posts at Yamagata Prefectural Yonezawa Women's Junior College (1993–2000), Koshien Junior College (president, 2000–2012), and Ryukoku University (professor, 2013–2021).
Yoshinobu Sakade (1934–2020) was a scholar of Sinology and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University and under Mitsuji Fukunaga before serving at Kansai University from circa 1974 to 2005.

Yoshinori Takeuchi (1913–2002) was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied at Kyoto University under Hajime Tanabe. He served as professor at Kyoto University (1959–1976) and Aichi Gakuin University (circa 1978–1988).

Yoshio Kawakatsu (1922–1984) was a Sinologist and historian who studied at Kyoto University and under Paul Demiéville. He held a library-related assistant post at Kyoto University from circa 1950 to 1984.
Yoshio Nishiguchi is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under Yoshitaka Iriya and Seizan Yanagida.
Yoshio Takeuchi (1886–1966) was a Sinologist and philosopher who studied at Kyoto University from circa 1907 to 1910. He held an academic post at Tohoku University from circa 1923 to 1946.

Yoshiro Imaeda is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University, EPHE, and Paris Diderot University under Rolf Alfred Stein and Ariane Macdonald. He held posts at CNRS, the National Library of Bhutan, and Kyoto University.

Yoshiro Tamura (1921–1989) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at the University of Tokyo and Toyo University. He held professorships at Toyo University (1965–1972), the University of Tokyo (1972–1982), and Rissho University (circa 1982–1989).

Yoshitaka Iriya (1910–1998) was a Sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University under Takeshiro Kuraishi. He held posts at Kyoto University, headed Chinese literature at Nagoya University (1955–1977), and was professor at Kyoto Sangyo University (circa 1974–1981).
